messages:
olivia: Quick FYI — I'm running a small canary for a new candidate (zephyrus-11b) with both int8 and int4 builds. Need a concise cost-vs-quality recommendation for GTN. TL;DR below.

rajesh: awesome — thanks. can you drop the bench numbers?

olivia: pasted microbench and eval snapshot: 
- perf (avg token latency, batch=1 on our g4x2): int8 38 ms/token, int4 12 ms/token
- throughput (tokens/sec): int8 ~26, int4 ~83
- unit cost (approx, normalized to hosted pricing): int8 ~$0.28 / 1k tokens, int4 ~$0.10 / 1k tokens
- quality (core GTN evals): short Q/A (<=64 tokens): int4 ~ parity (+/-0.6% acc). longform recall (>512 tokens): int4 drops ~5.6% F1 vs int8. hallucination rate: int4 +1.2pp on open-ended prompts.

hannah: noted. what's the slice distribution in prod? most traffic is short Q/A (~68%), longform ~12%, rest small chat multi-turn.

olivia: yep matches sample. short hits matter most for latency/cost. longform is expensive but lower volume.

matt: product question for @jordan — how bad is a 5.6% F1 drop on longform for GTN? is fallback acceptable?

jordan: for GTN search highlights, we can't tolerate large recall drops for long reads. fallback to int8 for long requests is acceptable if routing is reliable. primary ask: keep p95 latency under 200ms for short Q/A.

ellie: propose hybrid routing: route by token-length + confidence. quick rule: if prompt_tokens <= 64 -> int4; else -> int8. also add a cheap scoring pass to decide fallback for generated length > 256.

sam: can we do a soft rollout: 10% short requests to int4, monitor quality delta with auto-eval?

olivia: yes — rollout plan I had in mind:
1) Canary: 1% of total traffic (short-first) for 48 hours. auto-eval on GTN short/long slices.
2) Soft launch: 10% short Q/A -> int4 for 7 days, enable auto-fallback for >=256 tokens if internal scorer flags low recall.
3) Promote to 50% short traffic if no regressions.

rajesh: what about caching and KV behavior? int4 build has slightly larger kv-lookup overhead in our runtime which hurts very long sequences — observed ~+8ms at 2k tokens.

olivia: noted — we should keep long sessions on int8 by default.

matt: can you drop a minimal routing config for infra?

olivia: sure, quick config snippet: 
```
route_rule:
  - match: "prompt_tokens <= 64"
    model: "zephyrus-11b-int4"
  - match: "prompt_tokens > 64"
    model: "zephyrus-11b-int8"
  - fallback_policy:
      on_quality_flag: switch_to: "zephyrus-11b-int8"
      on_latency_violation: allow_int4_burst: true
```

ellie: add a sampling hook to mirror 1% of int4 traffic to int8 for offline diffing — very helpful for silent regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy request received for canary group 'zephyrus-int4-canary' (build: v2026.03.21-olivia). Canary will start in us-west-2 in ~4m.

sam: crosscheck cost math for GTN billing projections if we convert 60% of short traffic to int4.

olivia: rough econ calc (back-of-envelope): current short traffic cost at int8: 68% * baseline -> 
- baseline monthly tokens: 2.4B tokens
- short tokens (68%): ~1.63B tokens 
- cost int8: 1.63B/1k * $0.28 =~ $456k/mo
- cost int4: 1.63B/1k * $0.10 =~ $163k/mo
- potential savings if all short -> int4: ~$293k/mo (~64% reduction on that slice).

jordan: that's material. product wants conservative rollout but definitely pursue.

hannah: action items?

olivia: 1) start 1% canary (already requested) 2) add mirror to int8 for sample diff (ellie) 3) infra to implement routing rule + auto-fallback (matt) 4) prod to define acceptable longform delta threshold (jordan) 5) econ to compute expected billing impact under varied adoption (sam).

matt: I'll add the routing flag + canary filter in the next deploy wave.

ellie: will wire mirroring and the offline diff job.

sam: will do a sensitivity table by Fri. quick q — store the eval shots we use for canary somewhere reproducible?

olivia: using /evals/gtm/zephyrus_canary_v1.json (private). I'll PM links.

rajesh: thanks — lean and actionable. recommend we document this as a short-run playbook for future int4 candidates.

olivia: agreed — will write a 1-pager and link to the canary artifacts.

jordan: thanks all. if canary looks good let's aim to reduce short-slice unit cost ASAP. :rocket:

sam: @olivia ping me when samples are in, I'll run the econ sims.

olivia: will do.
